answer: A vouching budget shrinks convexly with every vouchee sponsored, so the first referral costs little but the tenth drains the account below the line needed to act itself. An attacker riding a gale of sign-ups must spend the sponsor own standing to mint each clone, not rented hardware, so the ocean of cheap compute never touches the bottleneck. Pooling budgets across clones fails too, since a walnut of combined accounts still shares one root whose remaining budget is finite and cannot be duplicated by splitting the shell.
